UB: program can do anything. Common: null dereference, buffer overflow, signed overflow, use-after-free, data races.
.cpp.Language Internals.ADL.exp
Argument-Dependent Lookup (Koenig lookup): searches namespaces of argument types when calling a function.
.cpp.Language Internals.Name Mangling.exp
Compilers encode function signatures into linker symbols. Different across compilers => no ABI compatibility. `extern "C"` disables mangling.
.cpp.Language Internals.Macros.exp
Preprocessor directives (`#define`, `#ifdef`, `#pragma`). Text substitution before compilation. Modern C++ prefers `constexpr`, templates.
.cpp.Language Internals.Forward Declaration.exp
Declaring a symbol before its full definition. Reduces compilation dependencies, breaks circular references.
.cpp.Language Internals.Scope & Storage Duration.exp
Scope controls name visibility. Storage duration: automatic (stack), static, thread, dynamic (heap). `::` for global scope.
.cpp.Inheritance & Advanced OOP.Multiple Inheritance.exp
A class can inherit from multiple base classes. Syntax: `class D : public A, public B`. Can lead to diamond problem.
.cpp.Inheritance & Advanced OOP.Diamond Inheritance.exp
Two classes share a common base. Virtual inheritance (`virtual public`) creates one shared subobject.
.cpp.Inheritance & Advanced OOP.Virtual Tables.exp
Each polymorphic class has a vtable. Each object has a vptr. `virtual` function calls dispatch through vtable at runtime.
.cpp.Inheritance & Advanced OOP.Dynamic Polymorphism.exp
Runtime polymorphism via virtual functions and base pointers/references. Enables substitutability.
.cpp.Debugging.GDB Basics.exp
GNU Debugger: step through code, inspect variables, backtrace. Commands: `run`, `break`, `next`, `step`, `print`, `backtrace`.
.cpp.Debugging.Debugging Symbols.exp
`-g` flag embeds debug info (DWARF on Linux, PDB on Windows). Levels: `-g0` none, `-g3` extra.
.cpp.Debugging.Sanitizers.exp
Google sanitizers catch memory errors and UB. `-fsanitize=address` (ASan), `-fsanitize=undefined` (UBSan).
.cpp.Debugging.Performance Profiling.exp
Profiling measures where time is spent. `perf` (Linux), Google Benchmark, `gprof`.
.cpp.Compilers.Compiler Stages.exp
Four stages: 1) Preprocessing, 2) Compilation (C++ -> assembly), 3) Assembly (asm -> .o), 4) Linking.
.cpp.Compilers.GCC & Clang.exp
GCC (`g++`): mature, extensive optimization. Clang (`clang++`): faster, better error messages, great tooling.
.cpp.Compilers.MSVC.exp
Microsoft Visual C++: Windows-only, `/std:c++latest`. MinGW: GCC port for Windows.
.cpp.Compilers.Linkers & LTO.exp
Linker combines object files into executable/library. Link-Time Optimization enables cross-TU inlining.
.cpp.C++ Idioms.CRTP.exp
Curiously Recurring Template Pattern: derived class passes itself as template parameter to base. Static polymorphism, no vtable overhead.
.cpp.C++ Idioms.Non-Copyable Idiom.exp
Delete copy operations to prevent unintended duplication. Essential for RAII wrappers owning unique resources.
.cpp.C++ Idioms.Erase-Remove Idiom.exp
`remove`/`remove_if` moves elements to end, returns new logical end. Pair with `erase`. C++20 `std::erase` simplifies.
.cpp.C++ Idioms.Copy on Write.exp
Defer copying until a write is attempted. Less beneficial with move semantics.
.cpp.Date & Time.std::chrono.exp
Type-safe time library. `duration`, `time_point`, `clock`. C++20 adds calendar and time zones.
.cpp.Date & Time.Random Number Generation.exp
C++11 `<random>`: engines (mt19937) and distributions (uniform_int, normal). Better than `rand()`.
.cpp.Iterator & I/O Streams.Iterator Categories.exp
Five categories: Input, Output, Forward, Bidirectional, Random Access. Higher categories support more algorithms.
.cpp.Iterator & I/O Streams.iostream Deep.exp
Standard I/O: `cin`, `cout`, `cerr`, `clog`. Formatting with manipulators.
.cpp.Additional Libraries.OpenCV.exp
Computer vision library. Core: `cv::Mat`, `cv::imread`, `cv::imshow`.
.cpp.Additional Libraries.fmtlib.exp
Fast, safe formatting library. Basis for C++20 `std::format`. Type-safe, extensible.
.cpp.Additional Libraries.spdlog.exp
Fast, header-only logging library. Async logging, rotating files, multiple sinks.
.cpp.Additional Libraries.Protobuf & gRPC.exp
Protocol Buffers: language-agnostic serialization. gRPC: RPC framework using protobuf + HTTP/2.
.cpp.Additional Libraries.Boost.Asio.exp
Cross-platform networking and async I/O. `io_context`, `tcp::socket`, `steady_timer`.
.cs.Getting Started.What is .NET?.exp

.NET is a free, cross-platform, open-source developer platform. It includes .NET Core (modern), .NET Framework (Windows-only legacy), and .NET 5+ (unified). Choose the right runtime for your scenario.
.cs.Getting Started.Project Types & Templates.exp
.NET provides project templates via `dotnet new`: console, classlib, web (ASP.NET Core), mvc, webapi, blazor, xunit, maui, worker, and more. Each generates the right .csproj structure.
.cs.Getting Started.IDE & Editor Choices.exp
C# development works in Visual Studio (full IDE), Visual Studio Code (lightweight with C# Dev Kit), JetBrains Rider (cross-platform), or the CLI with any editor. The .NET CLI is universal.
.cs.Getting Started.Top-Level Statements.exp
C# 9+ top-level statements eliminate boilerplate Program class and Main method. The compiler generates them automatically, enabling script-like entry points.
.cs.Getting Started.File-Scoped Namespaces.exp
C# 10 file-scoped namespaces remove one level of indentation. Use `namespace X;` syntax at the top of the file instead of a block. All declarations in the file belong to that namespace.
.cs.Variables & Types.Primitive Types.exp
C# has built-in value types: integral (byte, short, int, long), floating-point (float, double, decimal), character (char), boolean (bool). Each maps to a .NET struct in System namespace.
.cs.Variables & Types.var & Implicit Typing.exp

The `var` keyword tells the compiler to infer the type from the right-hand expression. It is strongly typed at compile time. Use it when the type is obvious from context, but prefer explicit types for public APIs.
.cs.Variables & Types.object & dynamic.exp

`object` is the universal base type (requires casting). `dynamic` bypasses compile-time type checking and resolves at runtime. Use `dynamic` sparingly — it sacrifices safety for flexibility (COM, JSON, DLR scenarios).
.cs.Variables & Types.Nullable Value Types.exp
Value types (structs) can be made nullable with the `?` suffix (e.g., int?, bool?). Nullable<T> wraps the value with HasValue/Value properties. Use null-conditional operators to handle null safely.
.cs.Variables & Types.Nullable Reference Types.exp

C# 8+ nullable reference types enable compile-time null-state analysis. Types are non-nullable by default; use `?` suffix to allow null. Enable via `#nullable enable` or in .csproj. The compiler emits warnings for unsafe dereferences.
.cs.Variables & Types.Null-Forgiving Operator.exp
The `!` postfix operator (null-forgiving / dammit operator) suppresses nullable warnings when you know a value isn't null despite the compiler's analysis. Use cautiously.
.cs.Variables & Types.Constants & Readonly.exp
`const` is a compile-time constant (implicitly static, no modifiers). `readonly` is a runtime constant set in the constructor. `static readonly` is like a constant that can be computed at runtime.
.cs.Variables & Types.Tuple Types.exp
C# 7+ tuples provide lightweight multi-value grouping with named fields. ValueTuple structs avoid heap allocation. Tuples are great for internal use; prefer records for public APIs.
.cs.Operators.Arithmetic & Assignment.exp

Standard arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, %) work on numeric types. Assignment can be combined (+=, -=, etc.). The increment (++) and decrement (--) operators have prefix/postfix forms with different evaluation order.
.cs.Operators.Comparison & Equality.exp

Comparison operators (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=) work on value types. For reference types, == compares references by default; override Equals and == for value semantics. Records have built-in value equality.
.cs.Operators.Logical & Bitwise.exp

Logical operators (&&, ||, !) short-circuit. Bitwise operators (&, |, ^, ~, <<, >>) operate on integer bits. Use `&&` instead of `&` and `||` instead of `|` for boolean logic to benefit from short-circuit evaluation.
.cs.Operators.Null-Conditional Operator.exp
The `?.` operator safely accesses members of a possibly-null expression. It short-circuits to null if the left operand is null. Chain multiple `?.` or combine with `??` for fallback values.
.cs.Operators.Null-Coalescing Operators.exp
`??` returns the left operand if it's not null, otherwise the right operand. `??=` (C# 8+) assigns the right operand to the left only if the left is null. Both short-circuit.
.cs.Operators.Switch Expressions.exp

C# 8+ switch expressions provide concise, expression-based pattern matching. Unlike switch statements, they produce a value. Supports type patterns, when guards, property patterns, discards, and relational patterns.
.cs.Operators.Conditional Operator.exp
The ternary `?:` operator evaluates a boolean condition and returns one of two expressions. Use for inline conditional values; avoid nesting for readability.
.cs.Control Flow.if / else if / else.exp
Standard conditional branching. Use `if` for boolean conditions, chain with `else if` for multiple paths, and `else` as the fallback. Can use pattern matching in conditions with `is` expressions.
.cs.Control Flow.Switch Statement.exp

Switch statements evaluate an expression against multiple case patterns. C# 7+ added type patterns, when guards, and the `_` discard. Cases can fall through with `goto case`, but typically each case has a `break`.
.cs.Control Flow.Pattern Matching.exp

C# pattern matching includes type patterns, property patterns, positional patterns (with deconstruction), var patterns, discard patterns, relational patterns (`<`, `>`, `>=`), and logical patterns (`and`, `or`, `not`).
.cs.Control Flow.for Loop.exp

The classic `for` loop uses an initializer, condition, and iterator. Perfect for indexed iteration, reverse loops, and scenarios where the iteration count is known. Declare the counter variable inline for scoped access.
.cs.Control Flow.foreach Loop.exp
`foreach` iterates over any type implementing IEnumerable or IEnumerable<T>. The iterator variable is read-only inside the loop. For arrays, the compiler optimizes with a `for` loop internally.
.cs.Control Flow.while & do-while.exp
`while` checks the condition before each iteration (zero or more runs). `do-while` checks after (always runs at least once). Use when the iteration count isn't known upfront.
.cs.Control Flow.break, continue, goto.exp
`break` exits the current loop. `continue` skips to the next iteration. `goto` jumps to a labeled statement (use rarely). `return` exits the method entirely. Use `break` in loops and switch cases.
.cs.Control Flow.using Declaration.exp
C# 8+ using declarations automatically dispose resources when the variable goes out of scope. Eliminates the nesting of traditional `using` statements. Works with IDisposable and IAsyncDisposable.
.cs.Methods.Method Basics.exp

Methods encapsulate reusable logic. They have a signature (name, return type, parameters), a body, and an access modifier. C# supports method overloading (same name, different parameters). Methods can be static or instance.
.cs.Methods.Parameter Modifiers (ref, in, out).exp

`ref` passes a reference to the variable (read-write). `in` passes by reference but is read-only (avoids copying for large structs). `out` passes by reference for returning values; the method must assign it before returning.
.cs.Methods.params Keyword.exp
The `params` keyword allows a variable number of arguments. The parameter must be a single-dimensional array and must be the last parameter. The compiler generates the array automatically.
.cs.Methods.Optional & Named Parameters.exp

Optional parameters have default values and can be omitted. Named arguments let you specify parameters by name, enabling skipping optional ones and improving readability for boolean/optional parameters.
.cs.Methods.Expression-Bodied Members.exp
C# 6+ expression-bodied members use `=>` for concise single-expression methods, properties, and operators. Available for methods, get-only properties, constructors, finalizers, and operators.
.cs.Methods.Local Functions.exp

C# 7+ local functions are nested methods inside another method. They capture variables from the enclosing scope, support generics, async, and even attributes. Great for helper logic that shouldn't leak.
.cs.Methods.Return Values & Multiple Returns.exp

Methods return a single value. Return multiple values using tuples, out parameters, or a custom class/record. Tuples are lightweight; records are better for public APIs. Use `ValueTuple` for zero-allocation returns.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Classes & Objects.exp

Classes are reference types that serve as blueprints for objects. They encapsulate data (fields, properties) and behavior (methods). Use `new` to create instances. Classes support inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Fields & Properties.exp

Fields store internal state. Properties expose fields with get/set accessors, enabling validation, computed values, and lazy initialization. Auto-properties generate backing fields automatically (C# 3+).
.cs.Classes & OOP.Init Setters & Required Members.exp

C# 9 `init` setters enable object initializer-only property assignment (immutable after construction). C# 11 `required` members force callers to provide a value during initialization. Both support object/collection initializer patterns.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Primary Constructors.exp

C# 12 primary constructors allow parameter declaration directly on the class/struct/record. Parameters are in scope throughout the class body. For classes, they don't auto-generate properties (unlike records). Capture them explicitly if needed.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Record Types.exp

C# 9 records provide value semantics by default: positional construction, immutable properties (with init), value-based equality, `with` expressions for non-destructive mutation, and concise deconstruction. Use `record class` (reference) or `record struct` (value).
.cs.Classes & OOP.Inheritance.exp

C# supports single class inheritance. Use `:` to derive, `virtual` for overridable methods, `override` for specialization, `abstract` for forced implementation, `sealed` to prevent further inheritance. Base class constructors chain via `: base()`.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Polymorphism.exp

Polymorphism allows derived types to be treated as base types. Virtual method dispatch calls the most derived override at runtime. Interface polymorphism enables unrelated types to share contracts. Use `is` and `as` for type-safe casting.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Abstract Classes & Sealed.exp

Abstract classes cannot be instantiated, serving as base types with partial implementation. `abstract` members have no body and must be overridden. `sealed` on a class prevents inheritance entirely; on a method it stops further overriding.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Static Members & Classes.exp

Static classes contain only static members and cannot be instantiated. Static members belong to the type, not instances. Static constructors run once per type before any static member access. Extension methods must be in static classes.
.cs.Classes & OOP.Object Initializers.exp
Object initializers set properties/fields at creation without requiring a constructor. Collection initializers add items inline. Works with `init` setters and `required` members (C# 11+).
.cs.Interfaces & Generics.Interface Basics.exp

Interfaces define contracts with methods, properties, events, and indexers. A class/struct can implement multiple interfaces. Interfaces enable loose coupling, polymorphism, and dependency injection. C# 8+ allows default implementations.
.cs.Interfaces & Generics.Default Interface Methods.exp

C# 8+ default interface methods allow adding members to interfaces without breaking existing implementations. Implementations can override the default. Useful for API evolution and trait-like patterns. Not available in .NET Framework 4.8.
.cs.Interfaces & Generics.Generic Constraints.exp

Constraints restrict type parameters: `where T : class` (reference), `struct` (value), `notnull` (non-nullable), `new()` (parameterless constructor), base class, interface, or `unmanaged` (blittable). Multiple constraints are stacked.
.cs.Interfaces & Generics.Covariance & Contravariance.exp

Covariance (`out`) allows using a more derived type in output positions (e.g., `IEnumerable<Dog>` as `IEnumerable<Animal>`). Contravariance (`in`) allows less derived input (e.g., `IComparer<Animal>` as `IComparer<Dog>`). Only applies to interfaces/delegates with reference types.
.cs.Interfaces & Generics.Generic Methods.exp

Type parameters can be defined on methods (not just classes). The compiler infers types from arguments. Generic methods enable type-safe algorithms without boxing. Combine with constraints for additional capabilities.
.cs.Interfaces & Generics.IDisposable & IAsyncDisposable.exp

IDisposable defines a deterministic cleanup pattern. The `using` statement ensures Dispose() is called even on exceptions. `IAsyncDisposable` (C# 8+) enables async cleanup with `await using`. Implement the dispose pattern properly for classes holding unmanaged resources.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.Arrays.exp

Fixed-size, zero-indexed collections of elements of the same type. Arrays are reference types with a fixed length set at creation. Supports multi-dimensional (rectangular) and jagged (array-of-arrays) forms.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.List<T>.exp

List<T> is a generic dynamic array that grows as needed. Provides O(1) index access, O(n) insert/remove at arbitrary positions. Use for ordered collections where size changes. Implements IList<T>, ICollection<T>, IEnumerable<T>.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.Dictionary<TKey, TValue>.exp

Dictionary provides O(1) key-value lookups via hash table. Keys must be unique and properly implement GetHashCode/Equals. Use TryGetValue for safe access. Use ConcurrentDictionary for thread-safe scenarios.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.HashSet<T> & SortedSet<T>.exp

HashSet<T> is an unordered set with O(1) add/remove/lookup. SortedSet<T> maintains sorted order (O(log n)). Both implement ISet<T> with set operations: UnionWith, IntersectWith, ExceptWith, SymmetricExceptWith.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.Queue<T> & Stack<T>.exp
Queue<T> is FIFO (Enqueue/Dequeue/Peek). Stack<T> is LIFO (Push/Pop/Peek). Both use arrays internally with O(1) amortized operations. Use for breadth-first vs depth-first processing patterns.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.LINQ Basics.exp

LINQ (Language Integrated Query) enables querying any IEnumerable<T> with SQL-like syntax. Query syntax (`from x in xs where ...`) or method syntax (`.Where().Select()`) produce the same IL. Deferred execution until enumeration.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.LINQ Methods Deep.exp

LINQ provides projection (Select, SelectMany), filtering (Where, OfType), ordering (OrderBy, ThenBy, Reverse), grouping (GroupBy, ToLookup), joins (Join, GroupJoin), aggregation (Sum, Average, Min, Max, Count, Aggregate), set ops (Distinct, Union, Intersect, Except), partitioning (Skip, Take, SkipWhile, TakeWhile), and element ops (First, Last, Single, ElementAt, DefaultIfEmpty).
.cs.Collections & LINQ.LINQ GroupBy & Joins.exp

GroupBy partitions sequences into groups with a key. Join performs inner joins on matching keys. GroupJoin creates a hierarchical result (left outer join). Zip combines two sequences element-by-element. All support custom equality comparers.
.cs.Collections & LINQ.Concurrent Collections.exp

System.Collections.Concurrent provides thread-safe collections: ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,T> (lock-free ops), ConcurrentQueue<T> (FIFO), ConcurrentStack<T> (LIFO), ConcurrentBag<T> (unordered), BlockingCollection<T> (bounded producer/consumer).
.cs.Collections & LINQ.PLINQ (Parallel LINQ).exp

PLINQ automatically parallelizes LINQ queries via `AsParallel()`. Uses partitioning and thread pooling. Control parallelism with `WithDegreeOfParallelism`, `WithExecutionMode`, `WithCancellation`. Results can be unordered (`AsUnordered`) for better performance.
.cs.Error Handling.try / catch / finally.exp

Structured exception handling: `try` guards code, `catch` handles exceptions (specific or general), `finally` always executes (cleanup). Exceptions bubble up the call stack until caught. Unhandled exceptions crash the process.
.cs.Error Handling.Exception Filters (when).exp

C# 6 exception filters using `when` keyword catch exceptions only when a condition is true. Unlike catching and re-throwing, filters don't unwind the stack. Useful for conditional handling based on exception data.
.cs.Error Handling.Custom Exceptions.exp

Create custom exceptions by inheriting from Exception. Follow best practices: end class name with `Exception`, implement the three standard constructors, use serialization if needed, provide additional properties for rich error data.
.cs.Error Handling.Guard Clauses & Argument Validation.exp

Validate arguments early using guard clauses. Use `ArgumentException`, `ArgumentNullException`, `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. C# 11 lets you specify the nameof parameter. Consider using `ThrowHelper` patterns or a library like Ardalis.GuardClauses to reduce inlining.
.cs.Error Handling.Throw Helpers.exp

Throw helpers are `static` local/member methods that throw exceptions. The JIT sees `throw` as a cold path and doesn't inline the helper, reducing method size and improving performance. Use for validation-heavy APIs.
.cs.Error Handling.Result Pattern (Functional Error Handling).exp

Instead of exceptions for expected failures, use a Result type to return success/failure explicitly. Common in domain-driven design. Integrates with `switch` expressions for exhaustive handling. Libraries like FluentResults or OneOf formalize this pattern.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.async / await Basics.exp

async/await enables non-blocking asynchronous code. async methods return Task, Task<T>, or ValueTask<T>. Await suspends the method without blocking the thread. Use ConfigureAwait(false) in library code to avoid capturing SynchronizationContext.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.Task & Task<T>.exp

Task represents an async operation. Task<T> produces a value. Tasks can be awaited, combined (WhenAll, WhenAny), or continued (ContinueWith, but prefer await). Status tracks lifecycle: Created, WaitingForActivation, RanToCompletion, Faulted, Canceled.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.Cancellation.exp

CancellationToken from CancellationTokenSource enables cooperative cancellation. Pass to async methods. Throw OperationCanceledException when cancelled. Use Register for callbacks. Linked tokens combine multiple sources.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.ValueTask & ValueTask<T>.exp

ValueTask<T> (C# 7+) is a struct that can wrap a synchronous result or a Task<T>. Avoids allocation when the result is already available. Use only for hot paths where sync completion is common. Can only be awaited once (use AsTask() for multiple).
.cs.Async & Concurrency.Async Streams (IAsyncEnumerable).exp

C# 8+ async streams enable async iteration with `await foreach`. Methods return `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` using `yield return` with `await`. Supports CancellationToken, ConfigureAwait, and LINQ via System.Linq.Async.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.Channel<T>.exp

System.Threading.Channels provides thread-safe producer/consumer queues. Bounded channels (backpressure) limit capacity; unbounded grow indefinitely. ChannelReader exposes ReadAllAsync() for async streams. Perfect for pub/sub and pipeline patterns.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.Task Parallel Library (Dataflow).exp

System.Threading.Tasks.Dataflow provides actor-like message passing blocks: BufferBlock<T>, ActionBlock<T>, TransformBlock<TInput,TOutput>, BatchBlock<T>, JoinBlock<T1,T2>. Link blocks into pipelines with completion propagation. Fine-grained parallelism control.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.Thread Synchronization.exp

Use `lock` for mutual exclusion (Monitor syntactic sugar). For finer control: Monitor (Wait/Pulse), Mutex (cross-process), Semaphore/SemaphoreSlim (counting), ReaderWriterLockSlim (read-heavy), Barrier (phased), CountdownEvent, ManualResetEvent. Prefer higher-level primitives.
.cs.Async & Concurrency.Parallel.For / Parallel.ForEach.exp

System.Threading.Tasks.Parallel provides parallel loops: Parallel.For (indexed), Parallel.ForEach (enumerable), Parallel.Invoke (multiple actions). Controls degree of parallelism and supports thread-local state (overloads). Use for CPU-bound parallel work.
.cs.File I/O & Serialization.File & Directory Operations.exp

System.IO provides File (static methods), FileInfo (instance), Directory, DirectoryInfo, and Path. Read/write text, bytes, or lines. Use async methods for I/O-bound work. Guard against path traversal and IO exceptions.
.cs.File I/O & Serialization.StreamReader / StreamWriter.exp

StreamReader/StreamWriter provide text-level access over streams. Support different encodings, buffer sizes, and async operations. Use `using` for proper disposal. FileStream provides raw byte-level access.
.cs.File I/O & Serialization.System.Text.Json.exp

System.Text.Json (high-performance, UTF-8) serializes/deserializes JSON. Supports source generators (AOT-friendly), custom converters, ignore/modify serialization via attributes, JsonDocument (DOM), and JsonSerializerOptions for configuration.
.cs.File I/O & Serialization.System.Text.Json Source Generators.exp

C# 9+ source generators for System.Text.Json eliminate runtime reflection. Declare partial classes with [JsonSerializerSerializable] (or [JsonSourceGenerationOptions]) for compile-time serialization. Enables native AOT, reduces startup, avoids reflection.
.cs.File I/O & Serialization.XML Serialization.exp

XmlSerializer serializes to/from XML. Control output with attributes ([XmlElement], [XmlAttribute], [XmlIgnore], [XmlArray]). Supports complex object graphs. XDocument/Linq to Xml provides LINQ-friendly XML manipulation.
.cs.File I/O & Serialization.Binary Serialization (obsolete).exp

BinaryFormatter (now obsolete/unsafe) serializes object graphs including private members. .NET 8+ throws PlatformNotSupportedException. Use JSON, Protobuf, or MessagePack instead. Never use BinaryFormatter in new code due to security risks (deserialization vulnerabilities).
.cs.File I/O & Serialization.Protocol Buffers (Protobuf).exp

Google.Protobuf provides compact, cross-language serialization via .proto definitions. Much smaller/faster than JSON. Use with gRPC. Generate C# classes from .proto files. Ideal for high-performance internal services and wire protocols.
.cs.Memory & Performance.Span<T> & ReadOnlySpan<T>.exp

Span<T> is a stack-allocated ref struct providing safe, allocation-free views over contiguous memory (arrays, strings, native memory). No heap allocation. Ideal for high-performance string parsing, buffer manipulation, and slicing operations.
.cs.Memory & Performance.Memory<T> & ReadOnlyMemory<T>.exp

Memory<T> is the heap-friendly counterpart to Span<T>. Can be stored in fields, async methods, and lambdas. Use Span<T> for synchronous processing, Memory<T> when the buffer needs to survive on the heap or cross async boundaries.
.cs.Memory & Performance.ref struct & readonly ref struct.exp

ref struct types are stack-only (cannot be boxed, used as generic type args, stored in heap, or be a field of a class). Used by Span<T>, ReadOnlySpan<T>. `readonly ref struct` ensures all fields are readonly. Enables safe stack-only memory handling.
.cs.Memory & Performance.stackalloc.exp

stackalloc allocates memory on the stack (fast, no GC pressure). Use with Span<T> for safe access. Available in unsafe and safe contexts (via Span). Be mindful of stack space (~1 MB per thread). Best for small temporary buffers.
.cs.Memory & Performance.Unsafe Code & Pointers.exp

C# supports pointer operations in `unsafe` blocks. Enables direct memory access, pointer arithmetic, and fixed memory. Use for interop and performance-critical code. Requires `/unsafe` compiler option. Prefer Span<T> over raw pointers when possible.
.cs.Memory & Performance.Ref Returns & Ref Locals.exp

ref returns allow methods to return references (avoiding copying). ref locals alias existing variables. `ref readonly` returns read-only references. Useful for performance in large struct manipulation and array-like data structures.
.cs.Memory & Performance.Memory Pool & ArrayPool.exp

ArrayPool<T> reuses arrays to reduce allocation and GC pressure. MemoryPool<T> wraps ArrayPool for Memory<T>. Rent and return buffers. Critical in high-throughput server applications (ASP.NET Core, Dataflow). Always return rented buffers.
.cs.Interop.P/Invoke (Platform Invoke).exp

P/Invoke calls native functions from DLLs using DllImport. Specify CharSet, CallingConvention, EntryPoint. Marshal data between managed and unmanaged memory. Use LibraryImport (source-generated) in .NET 7+ for better performance.
.cs.Interop.COM Interop.exp

COM interop enables calling COM components from .NET (and .NET components from COM). Use COM import attributes, RCW (Runtime Callable Wrapper). .NET 5+ improved COM activation. Common for Office automation, Windows shell extensions, and legacy COM libraries.
.cs.Interop.Fixed Size Buffers.exp

Fixed-size buffers (fixed keyword) define inline arrays in structs for interop scenarios. Used in unsafe context. The buffer is embedded in the struct layout, matching native memory layouts. Commonly used with P/Invoke and binary protocol parsing.
.cs.Interop.Marshal Class.exp

System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal provides methods for allocating/freeing unmanaged memory, converting between managed/unmanaged types, structure layout, COM interop, and size computations. Essential for low-level interop scenarios.
.cs.Testing.xUnit.net Basics.exp

xUnit is .NET's most popular test framework. Use [Fact] for parameterless tests, [Theory] with [InlineData], [ClassData], or [MemberData] for parameterized tests. Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) is the standard structure. Use IClassFixture for shared context.
.cs.Testing.NUnit Basics.exp

NUnit uses [Test], [TestCase], [SetUp], [TearDown], [OneTimeSetUp]. Supports assertions with Assert.That (constraint model), categories, retries, parallel execution. Classic assertions (AreEqual) also work but constraint model is preferred.
.cs.Testing.Moq (Mocking).exp

Moq creates mock objects for interfaces and classes. Setup method behavior, verify invocations, use Callback for side effects. Supports strict vs loose mocking (default: loose). Combine with It.Is<T>() for argument matching.
.cs.Testing.FluentAssertions.exp

FluentAssertions provides readable, self-documenting assertions. Supports chaining, object graph comparison, collections, strings, timespans, exceptions, and more. Integrates with xUnit, NUnit, MSTest. Produces detailed failure messages.
.cs.Testing.TDD with C#.exp

Test-Driven Development cycle: Red (write failing test), Green (write minimal code to pass), Refactor (improve code while tests pass). Tests drive API design. Use parameterized tests for edge cases. Keep tests fast, isolated, and deterministic.
.cs..NET Ecosystem.NuGet Package Manager.exp

NuGet is the package manager for .NET. `dotnet add package` installs packages. `dotnet restore` resolves dependencies. PackageReference in .csproj stores versions. nuget.config controls sources. Use Central Package Management for multi-project solutions.
.cs..NET Ecosystem.ASP.NET Core Minimal API.exp

ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs provide a concise way to build HTTP APIs with minimal ceremony. Use top-level statements, route handlers with dependency injection, and middleware. Perfect for microservices and simple endpoints.
.cs..NET Ecosystem.Entity Framework Core.exp

EF Core is an object-relational mapper (ORM). Models map to database tables via DbContext. Supports migrations, LINQ queries, change tracking, eager/lazy/explicit loading, and providers for SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite, etc.
.cs..NET Ecosystem.Blazor Basics.exp

Blazor builds interactive web UIs using C# instead of JavaScript. Blazor Server runs logic on the server via SignalR. Blazor WebAssembly runs compiled .NET in the browser. Blazor Hybrid embeds in native apps (MAUI, WPF). Components are .razor files.
.cs..NET Ecosystem.Dependency Injection.exp

ASP.NET Core has built-in DI with three lifetimes: Singleton (one instance), Scoped (per request), Transient (new each time). Register services in Program.cs. The framework auto-injects into constructors of controllers, minimal APIs, and middleware.
.cs..NET Ecosystem.Configuration & Options.exp

.NET supports configuration from JSON, environment variables, CLI args, and more via IConfiguration. Options pattern with IOptions<T> (reloadable), IOptionsSnapshot<T> (scoped, reloads per request), IOptionsMonitor<T> (singleton, observes changes). Strongly-typed settings with validation.
.cs.Advanced.Source Generators.exp

C# 9+ source generators run at compile-time to emit C# source files. Create an IncrementalGenerator implementing IIncrementalGenerator. Access syntax trees, semantic models, and attributes. Used by System.Text.Json, Regex, and MediatR for compile-time code gen.
.cs.Advanced.Compile-Time Code Generation with Roslyn.exp

Roslyn (the C# compiler platform) provides APIs for syntax analysis, semantic analysis, code generation, and compilation. Use CSharpSyntaxTree, SemanticModel, Compilation, and SyntaxGenerator to build or analyze code programmatically.
.cs.Advanced.Native AOT Compilation.exp

Native AOT (Ahead-of-Time) compiles .NET directly to native code (no JIT/IL). Enables fast startup, small self-contained binaries, no runtime compilation. Limited to compatible APIs (no reflection by default). Enable with `<PublishAot>true</PublishAot>` in .csproj.
.cs.Advanced.Function Pointers (delegate*).exp

C# 9 function pointers (`delegate*<T>`) enable efficient native-like function pointer calls without delegate allocation. Used in unsafe contexts for interop and high-performance callbacks. More efficient than delegates (no object allocation).
.cs.Advanced.Regex Source Generators.exp

C# 11+ Regex source generators ([GeneratedRegex]) compile regular expressions at build time. Eliminates runtime compilation (!), provides IntelliSense, and is AOT-compatible. RegexOptions regex options can be passed declaratively.
.cs.Advanced.Raw String Literals.exp

C# 11 raw string literals use triple quotes `"""..."""` for multi-line strings. No escaping needed for quotes, backslashes. Indentation is determined by the closing `"""` position. Perfect for JSON, XML, SQL, regex embedded in code.
.cs.Advanced.Interceptors (Experimental).exp

Interceptors (C# 12 experimental) allow a source generator to replace a method call with a different implementation at compile time. Used for advanced AOP scenarios. Requires `[InterceptsLocation]` attribute. Still experimental, could change.
.cs.Advanced.List Patterns.exp

C# 11 list patterns enable matching on arrays and lists in switch expressions. Supports slice patterns (`..`), discard (`_`), nested patterns. Useful for parsing, validation, and sequence matching without manual indexing.
.cs.C# 12 & .NET 8 Features.Collection Expressions.exp

C# 12 collection expressions use `[x, y, z]` syntax to create lists, arrays, spans, and other collection types. The compiler infers the type from the target. Supports spread operator `..` to inline other collections.
.cs.C# 12 & .NET 8 Features.Default Lambda Parameters.exp
C# 12 allows default parameter values in lambdas. Works with both lambda expressions and method group conversions. The default applies when the argument is omitted at the call site.
.cs.C# 12 & .NET 8 Features.ref readonly Parameters.exp

C# 12 `ref readonly` parameters combine ref (pass by reference, avoid copy) with readonly (guarantee caller's value is not modified). Best for large readonly structs. The caller provides data without defensive copies.
.cs.C# 12 & .NET 8 Features.Alias Any Type.exp
C# 12 global/using aliases can refer to any type, not just named types. Tuple types, array types, pointer types, nullable types — all can be aliased. Improves readability for complex type signatures.
.cs.C# 12 & .NET 8 Features.params Collections.exp

C# 12 extends `params` to work with `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, and `IEnumerable<T>` beyond just arrays. The compiler creates the collection efficiently with no allocation when using span overloads.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Small Methods (Fits in Your Head).exp

Mark Seemann's core heuristic: methods should fit in your head — at most ~10–15 lines. Small methods reduce cognitive load, simplify testing, and force good naming. Extract until you can't extract anymore; each method does one thing at one level of abstraction.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Command-Query Separation.exp

CQS (from Bertrand Meyer, popularized by Seemann) says: a method should be a command (mutates state, returns void/Task) OR a query (returns a value, no side effects), never both. This makes code predictable, testable, and safe to compose.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Pure Functions & Determinism.exp

A pure function always returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects (no I/O, no mutation). Pure functions are trivial to test, cache, parallelize, and reason about. Push side effects to the edges of your architecture.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Cyclomatic Complexity & Guard Clauses.exp

Cyclomatic complexity measures independent paths through code. Keep each method's complexity ≤ 4 (1 + number of decisions). Use guard clauses (early return) to flatten nesting. Extract conditional logic into well-named methods.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.API Surface & Information Hiding.exp

Minimize the public API surface of each type. Mark everything `private` by default, then promote only what external consumers need. Fewer public members = less coupling, easier refactoring, simpler testing. Apply the Interface Segregation Principle.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Property-Based Testing.exp

Property-Based Testing (from FsCheck for .NET) tests general properties/ invariants instead of specific examples. The framework generates random inputs to find edge cases. Properties like: roundtrip, idempotence, commutativity, and invariant preservation.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.SUT & Test Data Builders.exp

Test Data Builder pattern (from Growing Object-Oriented Software) constructs test objects with sensible defaults and explicit overrides. Avoids repetitive Arrange code, makes tests readable, and isolates test changes when constructors change.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Postel's Law & Defensive Coding.exp

Postel's Law: "Be conservative in what you send, liberal in what you accept." Accept flexible inputs (handle edge cases gracefully) but produce strict, predictable outputs. Use null checks, validation, and normalization at boundaries.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Dependency Inversion & Composition Root.exp

Depend on abstractions, not concretions. Build a Composition Root (the entry point of the application) where all dependencies are wired together. This enables unit testing with mocks, delayed decisions about implementations, and parallel development.
.cs.Software Engineering Heuristics.Parameter Objects & Immutability.exp

Replace long parameter lists (3+ parameters) with a parameter object. Using `record` types gives you immutability, value equality, and deconstruction for free. Parameter objects make call sites self-documenting and simplify method evolution.
.cypress.Getting Started.Install.exp
Cypress is an open-source end-to-end testing framework installed via npm. It includes its own test runner, assertion library, and browser control with automatic waiting.
.cypress.Getting Started.Test Structure.exp
Cypress tests use Mocha-style describe/it blocks. Tests run in a real browser with automatic waiting, DOM snapshotting, and time-travel debugging.
.cypress.Getting Started.Assertions.exp
Cypress bundles Chai assertions with should and expect syntax. Assertions automatically retry until the element meets the condition or times out.
.cypress.Getting Started.Config & Plugins.exp
Cypress is configured via cypress.config.js. The config file controls browsers, timeouts, baseUrl, video recording, and plugins for extending functionality.
.cypress.Selecting Elements.get.exp
cy.get selects elements by CSS selectors, returning a jQuery-wrapped element. It supports chaining and built-in retry-ability.
.cypress.Selecting Elements.find.exp
cy.find scopes the selection to descendants of a previously yielded element. It is ideal for navigating within a specific container.
.cypress.Selecting Elements.contains.exp
cy.contains selects elements by their text content, which is more resilient to DOM structure changes than CSS selectors.
.cypress.Selecting Elements.Best Practices.exp
Use data-* attributes like data-cy for robust selectors that resist CSS and text changes. Avoid brittle selectors tied to implementation details.
.cypress.Interacting.click.exp
cy.click simulates a mouse click on a DOM element. It supports options like multiple clicks, position offsets, and force-clicking hidden elements.
.cypress.Interacting.type.exp
cy.type simulates keyboard input into form fields character by character. It supports special keys via curly braces like {enter}.
.cypress.Interacting.select.exp
cy.select picks an option from a <select> element by value, text, or index. It supports multiple selection when the multiple attribute is present.
.cypress.Interacting.hover.exp
cy.trigger simulates hover events since Cypress lacks a native hover command. It shows hidden menus and tooltips.
.cypress.Network.Intercept.exp
cy.intercept spies on and modifies HTTP requests at the network level. It can stub responses, wait for requests, and assert on request details.
.cypress.Network.Mock.exp
Request stubbing returns static data instead of hitting the real server, making tests fast, deterministic, and independent of backend availability.
.cypress.Network.Wait.exp
cy.wait pauses test execution until a specific aliased network request completes. It can also wait for a specified amount of time.
.cypress.Network.Stub.exp
Stubbing replaces server responses entirely, useful for testing edge cases, loading states, and error handling without a real server.
.cypress.Network.API Testing.exp
Test API endpoints directly with cy.request. It bypasses the UI and allows testing backend logic, authentication, and data shapes.
.cypress.Fixtures & Data.Fixtures.exp
Fixtures are external data files (JSON, images, etc.) stored in cypress/fixtures. They provide realistic test data that can be reused across tests.
.cypress.Fixtures & Data.Custom Commands.exp
Custom commands wrap reusable logic into chainable Cypress commands via Cypress.Commands.add, improving test readability and reducing duplication.
.cypress.Fixtures & Data.Custom Commands with TypeScript.exp
Custom commands can be strongly typed using TypeScript. Augment the Cypress namespace for autocomplete and type safety.
.cypress.Fixtures & Data.Test Data.exp
Test data factories generate consistent, repeatable data for tests. Using beforeEach hooks ensures a clean state before each test run.
.cypress.Advanced.Screenshots.exp
Cypress automatically captures screenshots on test failure. Manual screenshots can be taken with cy.screenshot for visual documentation.
.cypress.Advanced.Videos.exp
Cypress records video of the entire test run. Videos are stored in cypress/videos and can be configured or disabled in cypress.config.js.
.cypress.Advanced.CI Integration.exp
Cypress runs headlessly in CI with cypress run. The Cypress GitHub Action or Docker image provides browsers and dependencies.
.cypress.Advanced.Accessibility Testing.exp
Use cypress-axe for automated accessibility checks. It scans the DOM for WCAG violations and integrates directly into your test assertions.
.cypress.Component Testing.Mount.exp
Component testing mounts individual components in isolation using cy.mount. It requires the @cypress/react or @cypress/vue adapter.
.cypress.Component Testing.Props.exp
Props are passed directly to the mounted component to test different states and configurations without needing the full application.
.cypress.Component Testing.Events.exp
Event callbacks can be verified using Cypress spies. cy.spy wraps a function and tracks whether it was called with expected arguments.
.cypress.E2E Patterns.Page Objects.exp
Page Objects encapsulate page-specific selectors and actions into reusable classes, reducing test duplication and insulating tests from UI changes.
.cypress.E2E Patterns.Real World.exp
Real-world E2E tests simulate complete user journeys like signup, purchase, or search. They test critical business flows from start to finish.
.cypress.E2E Patterns.Multi-Origin.exp
cy.origin enables testing across multiple domains, useful for OAuth flows, payment gateways, and third-party integrations.
.cypress.E2E Patterns.Debugging.exp
Cypress debugging tools include cy.pause to halt execution, cy.debug to log the current subject, and browser DevTools for interactive inspection.
.cypress.Dashboard & Cloud.Cypress Dashboard.exp
Cypress Dashboard records test runs, provides parallelization, flaky test detection, and video/screenshot history. Connect via project ID.
.cypress.Dashboard & Cloud.Parallelization.exp
Split test files across multiple CI machines to reduce test suite duration. Requires Cypress Dashboard for orchestration.
.cypress.Dashboard & Cloud.Flaky Test Detection].exp
Cypress Cloud automatically detects flaky tests by analyzing test history. It provides flakiness scores and auto-retries for unreliable tests.
.django.Getting Started.What is Django.exp

Django is a high-level Python web framework that encourages rapid development with a clean, pragmatic design. It follows the 'batteries-included' philosophy, providing ORM, admin panel, authentication, forms, templates, and more out of the box. Django uses the MTV (Model-Template-View) architectural pattern, which is similar to MVC but with different naming. It emphasizes DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principles and security by default.
.django.Getting Started.Project Structure.exp

A Django project consists of a project directory and one or more apps. The project contains settings, root URL configuration, and WSGI/ASGI configuration. Apps are reusable modules that contain models, views, templates, and static files. The manage.py script is a command-line utility for administrative tasks. key files: settings.py (configuration), urls.py (URL routing), wsgi.py (deployment entry), asgi.py (async deployment entry). Each app has its own migrations, admin, tests, and apps configuration.
.django.Getting Started.Settings & Configuration.exp

Django settings control every aspect of the framework. Key settings: INSTALLED_APPS (list of enabled apps), MIDDLEWARE (request/response processing pipeline), DATABASES (database configuration), TEMPLATES (template engine config), STATIC_URL/STATIC_ROOT (static files), MEDIA_URL/MEDIA_ROOT (user uploads). Use python-decouple or django-environ for environment variables. SECRET_KEY must be kept secret. DEBUG=False in production. ALLOWED_HOSTS restricts domain names.
.django.Models & Databases.Defining Models.exp

Models are Python classes that define the structure of your database tables. Each model maps to a single database table, and each attribute maps to a database column. Django automatically creates the table schema, manages relationships (ForeignKey, ManyToManyField, OneToOneField), and provides a powerful QuerySet API. Common field types: CharField, IntegerField, BooleanField, DateField, DateTimeField, TextField, EmailField, URLField, FileField, ImageField. Field options: null, blank, default, unique, choices, verbose_name, help_text.
.django.Models & Databases.Migrations.exp

Migrations are Django's way of propagating model changes to the database schema. They're Python files that describe database operations. Key commands: makemigrations (creates migration files), migrate (applies migrations), sqlmigrate (shows SQL), showmigrations (lists migrations). Migrations track dependencies and can be merged. Always create migrations after changing models. Use --name for custom migration names. For data migrations, create empty migration and use RunPython.
.django.Models & Databases.QuerySet API.exp

QuerySets are lazy database lookups that allow chaining filters. They are evaluated only when iterated, sliced, or converted to list. Key methods: all(), filter(), exclude(), get(), create(), update(), delete(), order_by(), values(), values_list(), select_related(), prefetch_related(), annotate(), aggregate(), distinct(), count(), exists(), first(), last(), latest(), earliest(). Field lookups: exact, iexact, contains, icontains, in, gt, gte, lt, lte, startswith, endswith, range, date, year, month, day, isnull, regex, iregex.
.django.Models & Databases.Relationships.exp

Django supports three relationship types: ForeignKey (many-to-one), ManyToManyField (many-to-many), and OneToOneField (one-to-one). ForeignKey requires on_delete option (CASCADE, PROTECT, SET_NULL, SET_DEFAULT, SET(), DO_NOTHING, RESTRICT). related_name defines reverse relation name (default: modelname_set). ManyToManyField can use through for intermediary models with extra fields. OneToOneField extends another model (like inheritance). Generic Foreign Keys allow relations to any model.
.django.Views & URLs.Function-Based Views.exp

Function-based views (FBVs) are simple Python functions that take an HttpRequest and return an HttpResponse. They are the most straightforward way to handle requests. The function receives the request object and optional URL parameters. Returns HttpResponse, render(), redirect(), or JsonResponse. Can be decorated with @login_required, @require_http_methods, @csrf_exempt, etc. Simple and explicit but can become repetitive for CRUD operations.
.django.Views & URLs.Class-Based Views.exp

Class-based views (CBVs) organize view logic into reusable classes. Django provides generic CBVs: ListView, DetailView, CreateView, UpdateView, DeleteView, FormView, TemplateView, RedirectView. CBVs use attributes and methods for configuration: model, template_name, context_object_name, form_class, success_url, paginate_by. Override methods: get_queryset(), get_context_data(), form_valid(), get_success_url(). Mixins allow combining reusable behavior. CBVs reduce boilerplate for CRUD but have a steeper learning curve.
.django.Views & URLs.URL Configuration.exp

URL configuration maps URL patterns to views using django.urls.path() and re_path(). Each URL pattern has a route, view, optional kwargs, and a unique name. Include() allows nesting app URL configs. path converters: str, int, slug, uuid, path. Custom path converters can be defined. Use namespacing with app_name and include with namespace. The {% url %} template tag reverses URL names. For complex patterns, use re_path() with regex. Always name your URLs for maintainability.
.django.Templates.Template Language.exp

Django template language uses {{ variables }} and {% tags %}. Variables can be attributes, dictionary keys, or list indices. Filters transform variables: date, default, length, upper, lower, title, pluralize, slugify, truncatechars, safe, escape, join. Tags control logic: {% if %}, {% for %}, {% block %}, {% extends %}, {% include %}, {% url %}, {% load %}, {% static %}. Template inheritance with {% extends %} and {% block %} is the most powerful feature. Context processors make variables available in all templates.
.django.Templates.Static Files.exp

Static files (CSS, JS, images) are managed via django.contrib.staticfiles. In development, use runserver. In production, use collectstatic to gather files. Configure STATIC_URL, STATICFILES_DIRS (additional directories), STATIC_ROOT (production destination). Use {% load static %} and {% static 'path' %} in templates. For user uploads, use MEDIA_URL and MEDIA_ROOT with ImageField/FileField. Whitenoise is a popular package for serving static files in production.
.django.Forms.Django Forms.exp

Django forms handle HTML form generation, validation, and processing. Form classes define fields with validation rules. Forms can be bound (with data) or unbound. Common fields: CharField, EmailField, IntegerField, BooleanField, DateField, ChoiceField, MultipleChoiceField, FileField, ImageField. Validators: built-in (required, min_length, max_length, min_value, max_value), regex, custom. Widgets control HTML rendering: TextInput, Textarea, Select, CheckboxInput, RadioSelect, FileInput. Form rendering: form.as_p, form.as_table, form.as_ul, or manual field-by-field.
.django.Forms.Form Processing.exp

Form processing follows a pattern: GET renders empty form, POST validates and processes. Check request.method, instantiate form with request.POST (and request.FILES for uploads), call form.is_valid(), access cleaned_data, redirect on success or re-render with errors. ModelForm.save() creates or updates a model instance. Use commit=False for pre-save processing. FormSets manage multiple forms of the same type. Inline form sets handle related model forms.
.django.Authentication.User Authentication.exp

Django's built-in authentication system handles users, groups, permissions, and sessions. The User model provides username, password, email, first_name, last_name. Extend via OneToOneField (Profile model) or AbstractUser (custom user model). Key views: LoginView, LogoutView, PasswordChangeView, PasswordResetView. Decorators: @login_required, @permission_required, @user_passes_test. Mixins: LoginRequiredMixin, PermissionRequiredMixin, UserPassesTestMixin. django.contrib.auth.urls provides all auth URL patterns.
.django.Authentication.Permissions & Groups.exp

Django's permission system assigns permissions to users and groups. Each model gets three default permissions: add_, change_, delete_, and optionally view_. Groups bundle permissions for role-based access. Check permissions with user.has_perm(), @permission_required, or PermissionRequiredMixin. Custom permissions can be defined in model Meta. The admin interface provides group and permission management. Object-level permissions require third-party packages like django-guardian.
.django.Admin Interface.Admin Customization.exp

Django's admin interface provides automatic CRUD for models. Register models with admin.site.register() or use @admin.register() decorator. Customize with ModelAdmin options: list_display, list_filter, search_fields, list_editable, list_per_page, ordering, date_hierarchy, readonly_fields, fieldsets, exclude, inlines. Enhance with actions, custom templates, and widget overrides. Admin has built-in authentication, permissions, and history tracking.
.django.REST API (DRF).DRF Basics.exp

Django REST Framework (DRF) is a powerful toolkit for building Web APIs. Install with pip install djangorestframework. Core concepts: Serializers (convert complex types to/from JSON), Views (APIView, ViewSets), Routers (auto-generate URL patterns), Authentication & Permissions. DRF provides browsable API, content negotiation, throttling, filtering, and versioning. Use ModelSerializer for model-based serializers, ReadOnlyModelViewSet for read-only endpoints.
.django.REST API (DRF).ViewSets & Routers.exp

ViewSets combine logic for multiple actions (list, create, retrieve, update, partial_update, destroy) into a single class. ModelViewSet provides all CRUD operations. Routers automatically generate URL patterns from ViewSets. DefaultRouter creates API root view. Custom actions with @action decorator. Filter backends: DjangoFilterBackend, SearchFilter, OrderingFilter. Override get_queryset, perform_create, get_serializer_class for customization.
.django.Testing.Testing in Django.exp

Django's test framework extends Python's unittest. Use TestCase for database-backed tests. Client simulates browser requests. Factory Boy creates test data. pytest-django is a popular alternative. Key assertions: assertEqual, assertContains, assertTemplateUsed, assertRedirects, assertQuerysetEqual. Tests live in tests.py per app or a tests/ directory. Run with python manage.py test. Use --keepdb to preserve test database between runs.
.django.Deployment & Production.Production Deployment.exp

Django deployment requires a production-ready web server (Gunicorn, uWSGI), reverse proxy (Nginx, Apache), and database (PostgreSQL). Environment variables for secrets. Use django-environ or python-decouple. Disable DEBUG, configure ALLOWED_HOSTS, use secure cookies, enable HTTPS. Static files served via Whitenoise or CDN. Media files served via Nginx or cloud storage (S3, GCS). Database connection pooling with pgbouncer. Caching with Redis/Memcached. Celery for async tasks. Sentry for error tracking.
.dk.Getting Started.What is Docker.exp
Containerization platform that packages applications with their complete dependencies into isolated units called containers.
.dk.Getting Started.Containers vs Images.exp
Images are read-only blueprints; containers are runnable, isolated instances created from those blueprints.
.dk.Getting Started.Docker Architecture.exp
Docker uses a client-server architecture with a CLI communicating via REST API to a daemon (dockerd) that manages images, containers, networks, and volumes.
.dk.Getting Started.Docker Desktop.exp
Desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux that includes Docker Engine, Docker CLI, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and a GUI management dashboard.
.dk.Getting Started.WSL2 Backend.exp
On Windows, Docker Desktop can run the Linux kernel inside a lightweight WSL2 VM for native Linux container performance without Hyper-V.
.dk.Getting Started.Daemon Configuration.exp
Dockerd behavior is configured via daemon.json, controlling storage driver, log driver, registry mirrors, insecure registries, and resource limits.
.dk.Getting Started.docker info.exp
Display system-wide information about the Docker installation, including OS, storage driver, CPUs, memory, and running container counts.
.dk.Getting Started.Lifecycle Management.exp
Create, launch, stop, and clean up container runtimes explicitly through Docker commands.
.dk.Getting Started.Listing & Inspecting.exp
List running containers with docker ps, all containers with -a, and view detailed metadata with docker inspect.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.Dockerfile Basics.exp
Instruction set for creating container images. Each instruction creates a layer in the final image.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.FROM Variants.exp
Choose base images wisely: alpine (5MB), slim (Debian minimal), distroless (language runtime only), or scratch (empty) for different size and security trade-offs.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.RUN Layers.exp
Each RUN instruction creates a new layer. Chain commands with && and clean up in the same layer to reduce image size.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.COPY vs ADD.exp
COPY copies files from context into the image. ADD does the same plus supports remote URLs and auto-extracting tar archives. Prefer COPY unless you need ADD's extras.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.ARG vs ENV.exp
ARG defines build-time variables (not in final image unless persisted). ENV defines runtime environment variables that persist in the final image.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.WORKDIR.exp
Sets the working directory for all subsequent Dockerfile instructions (RUN, CMD, ENTRYPOINT, COPY, ADD). Creates the directory if it does not exist.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.USER.exp
Switch to a non-root user for better security. Always create a dedicated user; never run containers as root unless absolutely necessary.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.EXPOSE.exp
Documents which ports the container listens on at runtime. It is documentation only — does not publish the port. Use -p or -P at runtime to publish.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.LABEL.exp
Add metadata as key-value pairs to the image. Used for versioning, maintainer info, and organization. Use with --filter for image queries.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.SHELL.exp
Override the default shell (Linux: /bin/sh, Windows: cmd) used by RUN instructions. Useful for Windows containers or custom shells.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.HEALTHCHECK.exp
Tells Docker how to test if the container is working. Docker checks the command periodically; exits with 0 = healthy, 1 = unhealthy.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.Multi-Stage Build.exp
Use multiple FROM statements to chain build environments. Copy only required artifacts to the final stage, drastically reducing image size.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.BuildKit.exp
Modern Docker build backend (enabled by default in newer versions) with parallel builds, secrets mounting, SSH mounts, and better caching.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.Buildx.exp
Extended build capabilities built on BuildKit. Enables multi-architecture builds, simultaneous builds for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, etc.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles.Cache Mounts.exp
Persist package manager caches across builds using BuildKit cache mounts, speeding up repeated RUN instructions significantly.
.dk.Images & Dockerfiles..dockerignore.exp
Prevent unnecessary files from being sent to the Docker daemon during builds, reducing context size and improving build speed.
.dk.Container Management.docker run deep.exp
The primary command to create and start containers. Supports --name, --rm (auto-remove on exit), --restart, -d (detach), --network, and many more flags.
.dk.Container Management.Interactive Mode.exp
Run containers interactively with -it (--interactive + --tty) for shell access, debugging, or one-off commands.
.dk.Container Management.Detachment.exp
Run containers in the background with -d flag. Re-attach with docker attach, or follow logs with docker logs -f.
.dk.Container Management.Resource Limits.exp
Constrain container CPU, memory, and disk I/O using --memory, --cpus, --memory-swap, and --blkio-weight flags.
.dk.Container Management.Logging Drivers.exp
Configure how containers send logs. Drivers: json-file (default), syslog, journald, gelf, fluentd, awslogs, gcplogs, and local (efficient).
.dk.Container Management.Restart Policies.exp
Control automatic container restarts: no (never), always, on-failure[:max-retries], unless-stopped (also restarts after daemon restart).
.dk.Container Management.stop vs kill.exp
docker stop sends SIGTERM (graceful shutdown, 10s timeout), then SIGKILL. docker kill sends any signal (default SIGKILL) immediately.
.dk.Container Management.update.exp
Dynamically update container resource constraints, restart policy, and other configuration on a running container without recreating it.
.dk.Container Management.rename.exp
Rename a running or stopped container without affecting its internal state, IP, or volumes.
.dk.Container Management.wait.exp
Block the shell until a container stops, then return its exit code. Useful for scripting and CI pipelines.
.dk.Container Management.Port Mapping Deep.exp
Map container ports to the host with -p (specific) or -P (random ephemeral ports). Supports IPv4/IPv6, multiple protocols, and ranges.
.dk.Container Management.Environment Variables.exp
Pass configuration via -e flags, --env-file, or ENV instructions in Dockerfile. Variables are isolated per container.
.dk.Networking.Port Forwarding.exp
Map isolated internal container ports onto host interfaces, enabling external access to containerized services.
.dk.Networking.DNS Resolution.exp
Containers on user-defined bridges resolve each other by container name or network alias. Docker embeds a DNS server at 127.0.0.11.
.dk.Networking.Network Drivers Deep.exp
bridge (default, NAT), host (no isolation), overlay (multi-host), macvlan (MAC per container), ipvlan (IP per container), none (isolated).
.dk.Networking.User-Defined Bridge.exp
Create custom bridge networks for automatic DNS resolution, network isolation between groups, and attach/detach containers dynamically.
.dk.Networking.Host Network.exp
Remove network isolation to run directly on the host's network stack. No port mapping needed; container sees host interfaces.
.dk.Networking.Macvlan.exp
Assign a real MAC address to each container, making them appear as physical devices on the network. Useful for legacy apps that require direct network access.
.dk.Networking.Ipvlan.exp
Assign IP addresses to containers sharing the host's MAC address. L2 mode (same subnet) and L3 mode (routing between subnets) supported.
.dk.Networking.Network Aliases.exp
Give a container multiple DNS names within a network. Useful for running multiple variants of the same service.
.dk.Networking.Container Networking Model.exp
Docker's CNM defines Sandbox (namespace), Endpoint (veth pair), and Network (bridge/overlay) as core primitives for container networking.
.dk.Networking.Overlay Networks.exp
Multi-host networks that span across Docker swarm nodes, enabling container communication across different hosts securely over VXLAN.
.dk.Storage.Named Volumes.exp
Persistent data directories managed by Docker, isolated from container lifecycle. Survive container removal and can be shared across containers.
.dk.Storage.Bind Mounts.exp
Mount a host file or directory into a container at a specific path. Changes are reflected instantly on both sides.
.dk.Storage.tmpfs Mounts.exp
Mount a temporary filesystem stored in memory (RAM), not on disk. Data is lost when the container stops. Ideal for secrets or cache.
.dk.Storage.Storage Drivers.exp
Manage image layers and container writable layers. overlay2 (default, modern), aufs (legacy), devicemapper, btrfs, zfs, vfs.
.dk.Storage.Volume Drivers.exp
Plugins that extend Docker volumes to remote storage systems: NFS, SSHFS, S3, Azure File, Google Cloud, REX-Ray, Portworx.
.dk.Storage.Backup & Restore Volumes.exp
Back up volume data using a temporary container that mounts the volume and creates a tar archive.
.dk.Storage.Bind Mount Deep.exp
Bind mounts can be read-only, create missing host paths automatically, and support SELinux relabeling with :Z or :z suffixes.
.dk.Storage.Permissions.exp
Container processes run as root by default, creating files owned by root on bind-mounted directories. Use --user or USER to match host UID/GID.
.dk.Compose.Compose File Structure.exp
YAML file defining services, networks, and volumes for multi-container applications. Version 3 targets Swarm; version 2 targets single-engine.
.dk.Compose.Profiles.exp
Selectively start services with --profile. Services only start when their profile is activated, enabling different environments (dev, test, staging).
.dk.Compose.Extends.exp
Inherit and override service definitions from another Compose file or within the same file, reducing duplication across environments.
.dk.Compose.depends_on Deep.exp
Control startup order between services. Supports condition: service_started, service_healthy (requires healthcheck), or service_completed_successfully.
.dk.Compose.Healthcheck in Compose.exp
Define container health checks in Compose. Automatically used by depends_on condition: service_healthy and by Swarm for rolling updates.
.dk.Compose.env_file.exp
Load environment variables from one or more files. Supports multiple env_file entries; values are available to the container at runtime.
.dk.Compose.Secrets in Compose.exp
Manage sensitive data (passwords, API keys, certificates) using Docker secrets. Mounted as files at /run/secrets/ inside the container.
.dk.Compose.Configs in Compose.exp
Manage non-sensitive configuration files (config files, nginx conf, etc.) similar to secrets. Mounted at the specified target path.
.dk.Compose.Deploy Section.exp
Swarm-only deployment configuration: replicas, update config, rollback config, restart_policy, placement constraints, resources, and endpoint mode.
.dk.Compose.Compose Watch.exp
Automatically update running containers when source files change (Compose 2.22+). Supports sync, rebuild, and restart actions.
.dk.Swarm.Swarm Init.exp
Initialize a Docker Swarm cluster, transforming the host into a manager node. Swarm manages services across multiple hosts.
.dk.Swarm.Node Types.exp
Managers run the control plane and Raft consensus (odd count recommended). Workers run only tasks. Nodes can be promoted or demoted.
.dk.Swarm.Raft Consensus.exp
Swarm uses the Raft algorithm to maintain a consistent cluster state across manager nodes. Requires at least 3 managers for high availability.
.dk.Swarm.Service Replication.exp
Deploy replicated services across Swarm nodes with --replicas. Docker schedules tasks evenly across available nodes.
.dk.Swarm.Rolling Updates.exp
Update services incrementally with controlled parallelism and delay. Supports automatic rollback on failure and health check gate.
.dk.Swarm.Secrets Deep.exp
Encrypted secrets stored in the Swarm Raft store. Only granted services can access them. Mounted as tmpfs files at /run/secrets/.
.dk.Swarm.Configs in Swarm.exp
Similar to secrets but for non-sensitive config files. Configs are stored in the Swarm Raft store and mounted into containers.
.dk.Swarm.docker stack.exp
Deploy a complete Compose application to Swarm as a stack. Stack name prefixes all service names for isolation.
.dk.Swarm.Swarm Mode Networking.exp
Swarm uses ingress overlay network for routing mesh, and can attach services to custom overlay networks for multi-host communication.
.dk.Swarm.Routing Mesh.exp
Swarm's routing mesh allows any node in the cluster to accept traffic on published ports and route it to a container on any other node.
.dk.Security.Seccomp Profiles.exp
Linux syscall filter (Secure Computing Mode) that restricts which system calls a container can make. Docker ships a default seccomp profile allowing ~300 of ~450 syscalls.
.dk.Security.AppArmor.exp
Mandatory Access Control (MAC) system that confines programs to a limited set of resources. Docker generates and loads an AppArmor profile for containers by default.
.dk.Security.Linux Capabilities.exp
Fine-grained privileges for container processes. Drop all capabilities with --cap-drop=all, then add only required ones. Avoid --privileged.
.dk.Security.Read-Only Root.exp
Mount the container's root filesystem as read-only. Writable paths use tmpfs or volume mounts. Prevents attackers from modifying the filesystem.
.dk.Security.User Namespaces.exp
Map container root (UID 0) to a non-privileged host UID, so root inside the container has no special privileges on the host. Enabled via daemon.json.
.dk.Security.Content Trust.exp
Verify image publisher identity and image integrity using digital signatures (Docker Notary). Only signed images can be pulled or run.
.dk.Security.Image Scanning.exp
Scan container images for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) in OS packages and application dependencies. Use docker scout or third-party tools.
.dk.Security.Secrets Management.exp
Never bake secrets into images. Use Docker secrets (Swarm), --secret (BuildKit build), --env-file, or dedicated tools like Vault.
.dk.Security.gVisor.exp
Container sandbox runtime (runsc) that adds a kernel between the container and the host OS, intercepting syscalls for stronger isolation.
.dk.Security.Security Best Practices.exp
Defense-in-depth: run non-root, read-only root, drop capabilities, enable content trust, scan images, use secrets, and avoid --privileged.
.dk.Monitoring & Logging.docker events.exp
Stream real-time events from the Docker daemon: container start/stop/destroy, image pull, volume mount, network connect, etc.
.dk.Monitoring & Logging.Prometheus Metrics.exp
Docker daemon exposes native Prometheus metrics at /metrics endpoint. Configure in daemon.json for cluster-level monitoring with Prometheus + Grafana.
.dk.Monitoring & Logging.ELK Stack with Docker.exp
Centralized logging with Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Kibana. Containers send logs via the gelf log driver to Logstash or directly to Elasticsearch.
.dk.Monitoring & Logging.cAdvisor.exp
Google's cAdvisor (container advisor) exposes real-time resource usage and performance metrics per container. Often paired with Prometheus.
.dk.Monitoring & Logging.Resource Monitoring Deep.exp
docker stats shows live CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O per container. Pair with --no-stream for a single snapshot.
.dk.Monitoring & Logging.Logging Drivers.exp
Containers can use different log drivers: json-file (default), local (efficient compression), none (no logs), syslog, journald, fluentd, awslogs, gelf, gcplogs.
.dk.Monitoring & Logging.Telemetry Logs.exp
View container STDOUT/STDERR output with docker logs. Supports tailing, timestamps, since/until filtering, and following.
.dk.CI/CD.Docker in Docker.exp
Run Docker inside a Docker container (dinD) for CI pipelines that need to build and push images. Use --privileged or mount /var/run/docker.sock.
.dk.CI/CD.Caching Strategies.exp
Speed up CI builds by caching layers. Use --cache-from to pull a previously built image and use its layers as cache. Combine with BuildKit.
.dk.CI/CD.Multi-Arch Builds.exp
Build images for multiple architectures (amd64, arm64, arm/v7) simultaneously using docker buildx. Use --platform flag and push manifest lists.
.dk.CI/CD.GitHub Actions with Docker.exp
Build and push Docker images in GitHub Actions workflows. Use docker/login-action, docker/setup-buildx-action, and docker/build-push-action.
.dk.CI/CD.Docker Layer Caching.exp
Preserve Docker image layers across CI runs. Use GitHub Actions cache or registry cache mounts to avoid rebuilding unchanged layers.
.dk.CI/CD.Build Cache Optimization.exp
Structure Dockerfiles for maximum cache reuse: install dependencies before copying source, use cache mounts for package managers.
.dk.Docker Desktop.Kubernetes Integration.exp
Docker Desktop includes a single-node Kubernetes cluster. Enable in Settings > Kubernetes. Use kubectl directly or via the Docker Desktop UI.
.dk.Docker Desktop.Dev Environments.exp
Create reproducible development environments from Git repositories. Docker Desktop clones, builds, and runs the project without installing tools locally.
.dk.Docker Desktop.Extensions.exp
Extend Docker Desktop functionality with marketplace extensions: disk usage analyzers, secret managers, database GUIs, Prometheus/Grafana, and more.
.dk.Docker Desktop.Resource Settings.exp
Configure CPU, memory, swap, and disk image size for Docker Desktop's VM. Adjust based on workload needs (default: 2 CPUs, 8GB RAM, 64GB disk).
.dk.Best Practices.Image Size Optimization.exp
Minimize image size: use alpine or distroless, multi-stage builds, chain RUN commands, clean package manager caches, and omit debug tools.
.dk.Best Practices.Security Scanning.exp
Regularly scan images for vulnerabilities. Integrate scanning into CI/CD. Use docker scout, Trivy, Grype, or Snyk to detect and fix CVEs.
.dk.Best Practices.Dockerfile Linter (Hadolint).exp
Static analysis for Dockerfiles. Checks for best practice violations, security issues, and common mistakes. Integrates with IDEs and CI.
.dk.Best Practices..dockerignore Deep.exp
Exclude unnecessary files from build context to speed builds, reduce image size, and avoid cache invalidation from irrelevant file changes.
.dk.Best Practices.Tagging Strategy.exp
Use semantic versioning tags (1.2.3, 1.2, 1) plus descriptive tags (stable, latest, nightly). Avoid mutable tags in production; use digest pinning for immutable deployments.
.dk.Best Practices.Non-Root User.exp
Always run containers as a non-root user. Create a dedicated user in Dockerfile and use USER directive. This limits damage from container breaches.
.dk.Best Practices.Read-Only Filesystem.exp
Mount root filesystem as read-only to prevent attackers from modifying binaries or configuration. Use tmpfs for writable paths like /tmp.
.dk.Best Practices.Graceful Shutdown.exp
Handle SIGTERM properly in your application so docker stop can gracefully shut down. Use dumb-init or tini for proper signal handling.
.dk.Docker Internals.Namespaces.exp
Linux namespaces isolate containers: pid (process tree), net (network stack), mnt (mount points), uts (hostname), ipc (SysV IPC), user (UID mapping). Docker creates one namespace set per container.
.dk.Docker Internals.Cgroups.exp
Control groups (cgroups) limit and account resource usage per container: CPU shares/quota, memory limit/soft limit, block I/O throttling, and PID count. Managed by containerd via cgroup v2.
.dk.Docker Internals.OCI Spec & containerd.exp

Docker uses containerd (high-level container runtime) which uses runc (low-level OCI runtime) to spawn containers. The OCI spec standardizes image format and runtime configuration for interoperability.
.dk.Docker Internals.Overlay2 Storage Deep.exp
Overlay2 layers filesystem changes using Copy-on-Write. Image layers are read-only; the container adds a writable upperdir. Reads check upperdir first, then fall through to lowerdir(s).
.dk.Docker Internals.Veth Pairs & Bridge Forwarding.exp
Each container gets one end of a veth pair; the other end connects to the Docker bridge (docker0). The bridge forwards traffic between containers and to the host via iptables NAT/masquerade.
.dk.Docker Internals.iptables & NAT.exp
Docker manages iptables rules for container networking: MASQUERADE (outbound NAT to host IP), DNAT (port publishing), FORWARD policy, and inter-container traffic isolation.
.dk.Docker in Practice.Troubleshooting Exec.exp
Debug running containers with docker exec for shell access, process inspection, network diagnostics, and file system exploration without stopping the container.
.dk.Docker in Practice.Dockerfile Optimization.exp
Optimize Dockerfiles by: ordering layers from least to most frequently changing, using cache mounts, pinning base image digests, and removing build-time dependencies.
.dk.Docker in Practice.Multi-Stage Build Patterns.exp
Advanced multi-stage patterns: build-target selection with --target, copying from external images, using build arguments for environment, and distroless final stages for minimal attack surface.
.dk.Docker in Practice.Compose Development Workflow.exp
Use Docker Compose for local development with hot reload: mount source code as volumes, use profiles for dev services, and leverage Compose Watch for auto-restart.
.dk.Docker in Practice.Docker Build Secrets.exp
Inject secrets at build time without baking them into image layers using BuildKit's --secret flag. Mounted as temp files only during the build step, never persisted.
.dk.Docker in Production.Structured Logging.exp
Write JSON-structured logs to STDOUT/STDERR so Docker's logging drivers can forward them to centralized systems (Elasticsearch, Loki, CloudWatch). Avoid writing logs to files inside the container.
.dk.Docker in Production.CI/CD Pipeline Patterns.exp
Production-grade Docker CI/CD: multi-arch builds, SBOM generation, vulnerability scanning, image signing, and atomic rollouts with health check gating.
.dk.Docker in Production.Production Monitoring Stack.exp
Monitor Docker hosts and containers in production with Prometheus + Grafana + cAdvisor + Node Exporter. Set up alerting for container restarts, OOM kills, and resource exhaustion.
.dk.Docker in Production.Backup & Disaster Recovery.exp
Backup strategy for production Docker hosts: volume backups using temporary containers, Swarm state backup (Raft logs), image registry mirroring, and automated recovery procedures.
.express.Getting Started.Routing.exp

Routing defines how an application responds to client requests at specific endpoints (URIs) and HTTP methods. Express provides intuitive methods like app.get(), app.post(), and app.all() for route definition.
.express.Getting Started.Middleware.exp
